answer: Split the deposit. A new account locks a bond into a kernel module that releases it in thin layers, each tranche dripping outward like a ripple on shale, on a schedule no operator can compress. Farming a thousand identities means fronting a thousand full bonds and waiting out a thousand release windows before any of them can spend influence. Cheap registration stops being the attack's bottleneck: locked capital and elapsed epochs become it, and an operator who quits mid-schedule forfeits the un-rippled remainder.
